sections.h2: What does a house sale in Florence, KY involve?
sections.html:
A Florence seller picks between an agent, a private sale and a cash buyer, and Boone County's tax and recording offices sit behind all three. The city handles permits and rental rules, while the county assesses, bills and records.

Florence is a Boone County city in the Cincinnati metro area. The 2020 census counted 31,946 residents, which made it the eighth-largest city in Kentucky and the largest one that is not a county seat. The Census Bureau now estimates 34,018, up 6.4% from the 2020 base, a slower climb than Elizabethtown or Georgetown posted.

sections.h2: What do the Florence housing numbers show?
sections.html:
Florence has the oldest population and the steepest rents of the four cities, and its middle home value is second-lowest. In the 2020 count, 13,003 households lived in 13,624 housing units, 4.6% of them vacant, and the owner vacancy rate was only 1.2%.

With 10.7 square miles of land, Florence fits about 2,986 people into each square mile, the densest of the four. Median age in 2020 was 37.6, and 32.3% of households were one person living alone.

sections.h2: Where is Florence and what drives local demand?
sections.html:
Florence sits in eastern Boone County. U.S. 25, 42 and 127 pass through the center and run about 12 miles northeast to downtown Cincinnati. Interstates 71 and 75 cross the western side, with exits 178 through 182.

The settlement began as Crossroads, became Maddentown for a Covington attorney who owned a farm, then Connersville, and finally Florence because another Connersville existed in Harrison County. The Covington-Lexington Turnpike, finished in 1836, pushed growth along. Population was 1,325 in 1950, 5,837 in 1960 and 23,551 in 2000.

Employers inside the city include St. Elizabeth Healthcare, Boone County Schools, Robert Bosch, Walmart, Costco and the city government. Celanese, Citigroup, Kellogg's and Givaudan operate from addresses just outside the limits. The "Florence Y'all" water tower, built in 1974, is visible from I-71 and I-75, the Florence Y'alls baseball team plays at Thomas More Stadium, and Turfway Park racetrack lies inside the city. Retail sales reached $69,438 per resident in 2022, ahead of every other city in this group.

The commuter profile is distinct. Workers average 23.3 minutes to work, the longest of the four cities, and 63.2% of residents 16 and older are in the labor force. Accommodation and food service sales were $307.5 million in 2022, the largest total in the group. About 9.4% of residents were born abroad and 13.3% speak another language at home, the highest shares of the four, and 91.6% of households have a broadband subscription.

sections.h2: Which schools and services does Florence have?
sections.html:
Boone County Schools is the public district for Florence, and Gateway Community and Technical College keeps a campus south of town.

  • A Boone County Public Library branch operates in the city.
  • The Census poverty rate is 9.5%, the lowest of the four cities.
  • Households average 2.31 people, against 2.56 in Georgetown.

sections.h2: What goes on a Boone County tax bill for a Florence house?
sections.html:
Boone County describes seven lines on every bill. They cover the state, the county, the schools, the extension district, the library, the Northern Kentucky Health Department and a fire district. Florence owners also pay a city property tax, plus a flat $75 a year for each occupied dwelling to fund the 911 system, a fee that started in 2018.

Bills reach owners each October. Two things set the amount: the assessed value from the state's PVA office and the rate each taxing entity adopts. The Fiscal Court sets only the county's share. Read the payment dates printed on your own bill, or ask the Boone County Sheriff. After April 15, unpaid bills sit with the county clerk carrying a 10% penalty, a sheriff's add-on fee and interest of 1% for each month.

sections.h2: Can I challenge a Florence assessment before selling?
sections.html:
You can, though the calendar is short. Kentucky's Department of Revenue lays out the path:

  • The tax roll is open to the public for 13 days starting the first Monday in May.
  • Meet with the PVA or a deputy first, because no appeal can be filed without that conference.
  • File at the county clerk's office before the next working day ends once inspection closes.
  • Expect the local assessment appeals board 25 to 35 days later, and bring sales listings, building costs, insurance policies and a description of the property, since an appeal without evidence is denied.
  • Skipping the hearing after filing closes the door on the Kentucky Claims Commission.

Homeowners past 65, and owners with a total disability, can also ask the PVA for a homestead reduction. It takes $49,100 off the assessed value for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years.

sections.h2: How do short-term rental rules affect a Florence sale?
sections.html:
If your house has hosted overnight guests, the city permit does not go to the buyer. Florence treats any stay under 30 consecutive days as a short-term rental, wants one permit for each property, and issues it only to the named applicant at that address.

  • The fee is $500 and the host needs $1,000,000 in liability coverage.
  • Most residential zones allow the use only as a conditional use, and the Boone County Planning Commission issues that permit before the city acts.
  • Conditional-use rentals must be 1,000 feet apart, a rule that does not apply in the Main Street Overlay District.
  • Guests are capped at two per bedroom plus two, and concerts or weddings are banned.

The city lists 859-647-5413 for rental questions. Buyers who want the same use must start their own application.

sections.h2: What will a Florence sale cost the seller?
sections.html: The deed tax under KRS 142.050 is $0.50 per $500 block of value. For a $210,700 house, 422 blocks produce about $211, which the clerk collects as the deed is entered in the county record. Mortgage payoff, repairs and the seller's slice of the year's property tax usually cost far more, so request a payoff letter and the current bill before you weigh offers.

sections.h2: What paperwork should a Florence seller gather before accepting an offer?
sections.html:
A cleaner file shortens the time between acceptance and the deed.

  • The latest Boone County bill, showing the city line and the $75 911 fee.
  • A lender payoff letter dated close to the planned closing day.
  • Any short-term rental permit, inspection form or insurance certificate.
  • Leases and deposit records when tenants live in the house.
  • Receipts and permits for roof, furnace and addition work done since you bought.

Give the closing agent these items on day one, and ask the Boone County Sheriff whether any earlier year remains open.

faqs.q: Do Florence owners pay city property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Boone County says owners inside incorporated cities such as Florence pay a city tax on top of the county's seven bill lines. The amounts are printed on your own bill.

faqs.q: What is the Boone County 911 fee?
faqs.a: A flat $75 a year for each occupied dwelling, whatever its assessed value. It began in 2018 and appears on the property tax bill.

faqs.q: Can a buyer take over my Florence short-term rental permit?
faqs.a: No. The permit belongs to the applicant at that address and cannot move to anyone else. A new owner applies fresh, and most residential zones also call for a conditional use permit.

faqs.q: By when must a Boone County assessment appeal be filed?
faqs.a: By the end of the working day after the inspection period closes, following a conference with the PVA. The roll opens on the first Monday in May for 13 days, and appeals go to the county clerk.

faqs.q: How much deed tax would a Florence seller owe?
faqs.a: Kentucky charges the grantor half a dollar per $500 block of value. A house valued at Florence's Census median of $210,700 owes roughly $211.
